sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: A modern office worker rarely spends more than a few minutes on a task before something interrupts it. A message arrives, a colleague leans over with a question, a reminder announces a meeting. Each interruption seems trivial, and most are answered within a minute. The real cost lies elsewhere. Studies of attention suggest that after a person switches away from a demanding task, it can take a considerable time to return to the depth of concentration that was lost, and that part of the mind remains occupied with the abandoned task even while it attends to the new one. A day broken into fragments may therefore be busy from morning to evening and yet produce little work of lasting value.

Organisations often treat this as a problem of individual discipline, urging employees to manage their time better. But the habits of a workplace are collective. If a reply within minutes is expected, no single worker can afford to switch off notifications without seeming negligent. Some firms have experimented with protected hours during which meetings are forbidden and messages need not be answered, and they report that difficult tasks are completed sooner. The lesson is not that communication is harmful, but that uninterrupted time is a resource, and like any resource it must be deliberately protected if it is not to be spent without notice.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: For a long time, history was written as if only kings, generals and ministers had lived. The chronicles that survived were commissioned by courts, and they recorded victories, treaties and the succession of rulers with great care, while the peasant who paid the tax and the soldier who died in the battle appeared, if at all, as numbers. This was less a conspiracy than a consequence of the sources: those who could write, or could pay others to write, left records, and those who could not left almost nothing that archives thought worth keeping.

In the last century historians began to read these same documents against their grain. A land-revenue register, compiled to tell a ruler how much he could collect, also reveals which crops were grown, how families divided their fields and when a village fell into debt. Court cases about petty theft preserve, in the words of witnesses, the rhythms of a bazaar. Oral testimony, songs and temple inscriptions have been added to the historian's materials. The result is not a history without rulers but a fuller one, in which the powerful are seen alongside the people whose labour made their power possible. Such history is slower to write and harder to summarise, yet it comes closer to the truth that every age was lived by the many, not merely governed by the few.

questions.q: The passage is mainly about:
opts: The hidden cost of interruptions and the need to protect focused time collectively.
The design of modern office buildings.
The rudeness of colleagues who interrupt one another.
The advantages of answering messages quickly.
questions.why: Main idea: interruptions have a 'real cost' and 'uninterrupted time is a resource' to be 'deliberately protected'.

questions.q: According to studies of attention, after switching away from a demanding task:
opts: Part of the mind stays occupied with the abandoned task.
The worker forgets the task entirely.
questions.why: Detail: 'part of the mind remains occupied with the abandoned task even while it attends to the new one'.

questions.q: Why, according to the passage, can a single worker not solve the problem alone?
opts: Shared expectations of quick replies make individual withdrawal look negligent.
Notifications cannot be switched off on office devices.
Individual workers lack any time-management skills.
Managers forbid workers from working alone.
questions.why: Inference: 'the habits of a workplace are collective... no single worker can afford to switch off notifications without seeming negligent'.

questions.q: The author's attitude towards workplace communication is that it:
opts: Is irrelevant to the quality of work.
Is useful, but must be balanced against protected, uninterrupted time.
Should be as rapid and constant as possible.
Is harmful and should be largely abolished.
questions.why: Attitude: 'The lesson is not that communication is harmful, but that uninterrupted time is a resource'.

questions.q: The word "trivial" in the passage most nearly means:
questions.why: Vocabulary: each interruption 'seems trivial' because it is answered within a minute.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most suitable title for the passage?
opts: History from Below: Reading Old Records Anew
questions.why: Main idea: the passage traces how historians began recovering ordinary lives by reading 'these same documents against their grain'.

questions.q: According to the passage, a land-revenue register can reveal:
opts: The songs sung at temple festivals.
Which crops were grown and when a village fell into debt.
The terms of treaties signed between rulers.
The names of soldiers who died in battle.
questions.why: Detail: it 'also reveals which crops were grown, how families divided their fields and when a village fell into debt'.

questions.q: The passage suggests that older histories neglected ordinary people mainly because:
opts: Historians deliberately conspired to hide the lives of peasants.
Rulers ordered every record of peasants to be destroyed.
Ordinary people refused to allow their lives to be recorded.
The surviving records were produced by and for those who could write or pay writers.
questions.why: Inference: 'This was less a conspiracy than a consequence of the sources: those who could write... left records'.

questions.q: The author's attitude towards the newer kind of history is best described as:
opts: Appreciative, while admitting that it is more demanding to produce.
Nostalgic for the older court chronicles.
questions.why: Tone: it 'comes closer to the truth', though it 'is slower to write and harder to summarise'.

questions.q: The phrase "read these same documents against their grain" most nearly means to:
opts: Reject them as forgeries made by courts.
Draw from them information their compilers never intended to give.
Read them in reverse order, from the last page to the first.
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: the register 'compiled to tell a ruler how much he could collect, also reveals' quite different facts.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: The patient said, “My head aches.”
opts: The patient said that my head ached.
The patient said that his head would ache.
The patient said that his head ached.
The patient said that his head had been ached.
questions.why: Present simple backshifts to past simple; 'my' becomes 'his'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: “She used to ____ up at five every morning.”
questions.why: 'Used to' (past habit) is followed by the bare infinitive. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: “Under no circumstances ____ the ward after 9 p.m.”
questions.why: A negative phrase in front position requires modal + subject. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: “Hurrah! We have won the match,” said the boys.
opts: The boys said with joy that they have won the match.
The boys exclaimed with joy that they had won the match.
The boys exclaimed that we had won the match.
The boys exclaimed with joy they won the match.
questions.why: Exclamations use 'exclaimed with joy that'; present perfect becomes past perfect. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Choose the correct conjunction: “I would rather die ____ beg for mercy.”
questions.why: 'Would rather ... than'. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Who became the first Indian to win the Grand Chess Tour, beating Fabiano Caruana in the final?
questions.why: The final was played at the Saint Louis Chess Club, USA. Aug 2026.

questions.q: Who led the Indian contingent as flag bearers at the opening ceremony of the 2026 Asian Games on 19 September?
opts: Neeraj Chopra and P. V. Sindhu
questions.why: Kabaddi star Pawan Sehrawat replaced shot-putter Tajinderpal Singh Toor as male flag bearer. Sep 2026.

questions.q: Who was the chief guest at Goa's Statehood Day celebrations held at Kala Academy, Panaji, on 30 May 2026?
questions.why: Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan attended on his first official visit to Goa. May 2026.

questions.q: The Goa, Daman and Diu Mundkars (Protection from Eviction) Act, 1975 protects:
opts: occupants of dwelling houses on another's land from eviction
questions.why: A mundkar lives in a house on the landlord's property.

questions.q: The first Konkani feature film, released in 1950, was:
questions.why: It was produced and directed by Al Jerry Braganza.

questions.q: Which became the first state to qualify for the second instalment under PM-RKVY after using over 75% of its first release?
questions.why: The Centre had released ₹335 crore to the state under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana. Jul 2026.

questions.q: The Mhadei Wildlife Sanctuary is in which taluka of Goa?
questions.why: The Mhadei (Mandovi) river enters Goa through Sattari.

questions.q: INS Samarthak, the indigenous multi-purpose vessel commissioned at Karwar on 16 October 2026, was built by:
questions.why: The Vice-President commissioned it; it has over 75% indigenous content. Oct 2026.

questions.q: The 79th session of the WHO Regional Committee for South-East Asia (September 2026) was held in:
questions.why: Adopted the Dili Declaration on human resources for health. Sep 2026.

questions.q: The anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule) was added by the:
questions.why: The 91st Amendment later removed the 'split' exception.

questions.q: Statements: All chairs are tables. No tables are desks. Conclusions: I. Some chairs are not desks. II. Some chairs are desks.
questions.why: Checked against every possible diagram of the statements: I must be true, II need not be true. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, …
questions.why: Squares of 6, 7, 8, …. Next: 121. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Geeta is the mother of Kavita. Kavita is the sister of Deepak. Deepak is the father of Sita. How is Geeta related to Sita?
questions.why: Draw the family tree from the statements; the answer is Grandmother. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Sunil walks 9 m West, then turns left and walks 4 m, then turns right and walks 4 m. Which direction is Sunil facing now?
questions.why: Follow each turn from the first direction: the last leg is towards the West. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 11:30?
questions.why: Angle = |30×11 − 5.5×30| = 165°. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: If 6 August 2022 was a Saturday, what day of the week was 30 August 2022?
questions.why: 24 days later; 24 mod 7 = 3, so count 3 days on from Saturday. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Find the wrong number in the series: 51, 56, 61, 71, 71, 76, 81
questions.why: In the correct series each term adds 5, so 71 should be 66. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: In how many different ways can the letters of the word BANANA be arranged?
questions.why: 6 letters with repeats: 6! ÷ 3! ÷ 2! = 60. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Suresh walks 6 m North, then turns left and walks 6 m, then turns right and walks 2 m, then turns left and walks 2 m. Which direction is Suresh facing now?
questions.why: Follow each turn from the first direction: the last leg is towards the West. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: The present ages of Sunil and Ajay are in the ratio 2 : 4. After 8 years the ratio will be 5 : 8. What is Ajay's present age?
questions.why: Let the ages be 2k and 4k: (2k + 8)/(4k + 8) = 5/8 gives k = 6, so Ajay is 24. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Samuel Hahnemann was born in 1755 at:
questions.why: Hahnemann was born on 10 April 1755 at Meissen, Saxony; he graduated MD from Erlangen in 1779 and later lived at Leipzig and Köthen.

questions.q: Deep depression with suicidal thoughts, mental dullness and destructive impulses are the mental features of which miasm?
questions.why: The syphilitic miasm is destructive both in tissue and mind: depression, dullness, suicidal and destructive tendencies.

questions.q: In Kent's first observation, a prolonged aggravation followed by a final decline of the patient means:
opts: the remedy was correct and cure will follow
the remedy was only a palliative
the patient was incurable and the remedy acted too deeply on a weakened vitality
the patient is oversensitive and proves every remedy
questions.why: Kent (Lectures on Homoeopathic Philosophy): prolonged aggravation with decline shows an incurable patient; the deep antipsoric set up destructive changes.

questions.q: Frequent, ineffectual urging for stool in an irritable, sedentary person who lives on stimulants and rich food calls for:
questions.why: Nux vomica: frequent ineffectual urging, passing small quantities, in irritable, zealous, sedentary people; Opium and Alumina have no urging.

questions.q: Thick, horny callosities on the soles, split nails and a sentimental mood in the moonlight indicate:
questions.why: Antimonium crudum: horny callosities and warts, cracked nails, sentimental in moonlight (Boericke).

questions.q: A sore throat that is better from swallowing solid food, a typical paradoxical symptom, is characteristic of:
questions.why: Ignatia, the remedy of contradictions: sore throat relieved by swallowing solids (Boericke, Allen).

questions.q: Plants for homoeopathic drugs should preferably be collected:
opts: from their natural (wild) habitat, in dry and clear weather
at any time and place, as habitat does not matter
from cultivated gardens just after rain
in wet weather when the plant is full of sap
questions.why: Wild plants from their natural habitat, gathered in dry weather, give the most typical and stable drug.

questions.q: The symbol 'Rx' at the head of a prescription comes from the Latin 'recipe', meaning:
questions.why: Rx abbreviates recipe, 'take', the instruction to the dispenser to take the listed ingredients.

questions.q: A concomitant symptom is best defined as:
opts: a symptom left over from a past illness
a symptom occurring along with the chief complaint without an obvious pathological link to it
the factor that makes the complaint better or worse
questions.why: A concomitant accompanies the chief complaint in time but is not explained by its pathology; the modifying factor is a modality.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, symptoms of the nails are found in the chapter:
questions.why: Nails are listed as part of the extremities, for example 'Extremities, Nails, brittle'.

questions.q: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) begins the digestion of:
questions.why: Ptyalin splits starch into maltose and dextrins in the mouth.

questions.q: After digestion, long-chain fatty acids leave the intestinal cells mainly as:
opts: fatty acids bound to albumin in the hepatic artery
free fatty acids entering the portal vein
questions.why: Long-chain fats are re-esterified and packed into chylomicrons, which enter the lymph via lacteals; short-chain fatty acids go to the portal blood.

questions.q: In hemisection of the spinal cord (Brown-Séquard syndrome), pain and temperature sensation are lost:
opts: on both sides below the lesion
on the opposite side, beginning a segment or two below the lesion
on the same side below the lesion
only at the level of the lesion on the opposite side
questions.why: Spinothalamic fibres cross within one or two segments, so pain and temperature are lost contralaterally; dorsal-column sensation and motor power are lost on the same side.

questions.q: The histological grading of a malignant tumour is based mainly on its:
opts: Degree of differentiation and mitotic activity
questions.why: Grade reflects how closely tumour cells resemble normal cells (differentiation) and mitotic count; size, nodes and metastases determine the stage.

questions.q: A deep-vein thrombus that reaches the systemic arterial circulation through a patent foramen ovale is called:
questions.why: Paradoxical (crossed) embolism occurs when a venous embolus passes through an interatrial or interventricular defect into the systemic arteries.

questions.q: Which of these is a WHO warning sign in dengue that calls for close monitoring or admission?
questions.why: Warning signs include abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, fluid accumulation, mucosal bleeding, lethargy, liver enlargement and rising haematocrit with falling platelets.

questions.q: Fever with conjunctival suffusion, calf tenderness, jaundice and acute kidney injury after wading in flood water during the monsoon suggests:
questions.why: Weil's disease is the icteric, haemorrhagic and renal form of leptospirosis; conjunctival suffusion and calf tenderness are typical.

questions.q: The third stage of labour extends from:
opts: onset of true labour pains to full cervical dilatation
delivery of the baby to expulsion of the placenta and membranes
full cervical dilatation to delivery of the baby
expulsion of the placenta to one hour after delivery
questions.why: The third stage is the placental stage; the hour after it is often called the fourth stage (observation).

questions.q: A child can copy a circle at about:
questions.why: Copying a circle is a 3-year fine motor skill; a triangle is copied at about 5 years.

questions.q: The first-aid management of an acute ankle sprain is summed up as:
opts: rest and hot fomentation for a week
questions.why: RICE reduces bleeding and swelling in the first 48–72 hours.

questions.q: The first aid for an animal bite with suspected rabies exposure is to:
opts: suture the wound tightly at once
wash the wound with soap and running water for about 15 minutes
cover it with a tight bandage without washing
questions.why: Thorough washing removes much of the virus; the wound is not sutured early, and vaccine with or without RIG follows.

questions.q: Deep bruising of soft tissues such as the breasts, pelvic organs or abdominal wall after injury or surgery calls for:
questions.why: Bellis perennis acts on deep tissue trauma, especially of the trunk, breasts and pelvic organs.

questions.q: Under the Bio-Medical Waste Management Rules, 2016, used hypodermic needles and scalpel blades go into the:
questions.why: Sharps, including needles, syringes with fixed needles and blades, go into the white translucent puncture-proof container.

questions.q: Regarding a dying declaration recorded by a doctor, which statement is correct?
opts: The accused must be present and may cross-examine
It is valid only if recorded by a magistrate
It must be made in the presence of a police officer
No oath is given, and the doctor should certify that the declarant was conscious and of sound mind
questions.why: A dying declaration needs no oath and no presence of the accused; the doctor certifies compos mentis. The dying deposition, with the accused present, is recorded by a magistrate.

questions.q: In the Asiatic cholera epidemic of 1831, the remedy Hahnemann advised for the first stage was:
questions.why: Hahnemann advised Camphor in the first stage and Cuprum or Veratrum album in the later stages of cholera.
